_README: MACHINE-READABLE DATA MODEL — the definition scripts/record.py enforces BEFORE writing, and scripts/validate_data.py checks after. Rationale: docs/adr-011-schema-enforcement.md.
_enums_note: ENUMS ARE NOT DUPLICATED HERE. scripts/validate_data.py owns them; record.py imports that module. Restating a value list in two files is the drift this whole repo keeps fighting.

research_log._note: ADR-031 B4 (design §26.3) — `find`/`result` are optional, added so `referral-resolved`'s nobody-found clause can require EVIDENCE that a search actually ran, never merely that a window elapsed (nobody-looked is not nobody-found). Every research step that runs appends one entry, whether or not it found anyone; a queued or refused step appends nothing.

messages._note: dev #83 — declared 2026-08-14. Load-bearing for your_move.derive_channel_last_touch (joins on involvements.person_id, ADR-031 B1), previously invisible to this file even though validate_data.py has enforced it structurally (independently, ~lines 193-252) since 2026-08-02. 'required' here is exactly what that enforcement demands UNCONDITIONALLY; it CANNOT express the anchor rule because 'required' is an AND list — see validate_data.py's own check for that. ANCHOR RULE (widened for dev #686 / public #139, jobsearch 0.62.0; no migration, since every row valid before is valid after): a message must anchor to SOMETHING — `opp_id` (a role), `channel_id` (a relationship: a warm intro, a recruiter thread), OR `person_id` ALONE when that person resolves directly in `people` (a message to a person about no role and no channel — a networking reply, a thank-you). It is refused only when `opp_id` and `channel_id` are both empty AND `person_id` is empty or does not resolve (a merged id is refused like any dangling FK). A person-anchored message opens a person-kind thread (keyed by the person id) in your_move.conversation_axis, so a reply to a stored person-only inbound reads `reply-owed`, never `unverified-cold`. An inbound's id is minted per message (its date is part of the mint, P3), so two inbounds from one thread are two rows. The `answers` rules below are unchanged. Unlike opportunities, nothing yet feeds this entry into the unknown-key guard, so 'fields' is not enforced against messages.jsonl today. `answers` (dev/audit 2026-09-02, Class B) is the reply relation as a key: the id of the message this one replies to — optional, must resolve, must answer a message of the other direction, must not precede it; validate_data.py enforces all four, m_0_36_0_message_answers backfills history where attribution is unambiguous. `resolves`/`resolved_by` (design-inbound-resolution.md §2, ADR-029) are the SAME shape one layer over: `resolves` names the `applications.id` this INBOUND message resolves; `resolved_by` names which of ADR-030's three tiers matched (req-id|url|company-single). Both optional (no migration backfills history — ADR-029's own open question closes as 'no migration'); never set alongside `answers` on the same row (a message either answers a person or resolves an application, never both); validate_data.py enforces the five rules design §2 states.

asks._note: dev #93 (public #21) - the hand-authored tail of Your Move and the Process Needs list, cut over from focus.md prose. An ask is OPEN until resolved_on is set; every view filters resolved rows out, so expulsion is structural rather than an editing habit. kind=role renders in the Your Move queue; kind=system renders in the System & tooling group. Not for anything derivable from a record: a role decision belongs on the opportunity (next_action_owner), a relationship touch on the channel (next_touch). resolves_when (dev #133 / public #22, optional) declares the exact recorded action that answers a decision ask - 'application' or 'outreach' on the linked opp_id - so record.py can resolve the ask IN THE SAME LOCKED WRITE that records the action; it requires opp_id (validate_data.py refuses one without the other, because a resolves_when that can never fire looks handled and is not). An ask without it stays on the detection path (check_action_claims.py). trigger_kind/trigger_ref (public #27, 2026-08-25, optional): what CAUSED this ask - same enum and same own-record resolution rule as outreach[] triggers (an 'application' ref resolves against the linked opp_id's applications[] and therefore requires opp_id); an ask generated by an application stays joined to it instead of staying correct only because a human remembered. kind=suggestion (dev #834, design-network-first.md 8.2) is a SUGGESTED row the owner confirms: `suggests` is `{store, op, id, fields, before}` (what would be written, and what the target held when it was suggested). Nothing writes the row before `record.py confirm <ask_id>`, which writes it and resolves the ask in ONE locked write; `record.py decline` resolves it declined. Only `record.py suggest` writes one.

commitments._note: dev #93 (public #21) - scheduled commitments, cut over from focus.md's 'This Week' prose. The This Week tab renders date >= today; meeting_check.py and watch.py reconcile calendar artifacts against ALL rows (a meeting next month is still reconciled). date may be the literal 'unresolved' - the migration marker for a commitment whose date could not be parsed - which renders as a loud defect, never silently dropped. who carries the counterparty tokens the date-collision check matches on; a date alone is not an identity. status (public #50, additive) is the lifecycle field: 'scheduled' or 'cancelled' - the 0.40.0 seed migration stamps 'scheduled' explicitly onto every pre-existing row.

resume_variants._note: public #26 - the DECLARED printed-resume set. The variant FILES are authored markdown (the candidate writes them; D5); this store is the record of WHICH variants exist, which buyer archetype each serves, and when each was last reconciled against presence/claims.md (the claim union, formerly resume.md). `status` is `active`|`retired` and `retired` is TERMINAL: an applications[] row may reference a retired variant forever (history stays resolvable), but an opportunity's `resume_variant` (the variant to SEND) must name an active one - validate_data.py enforces both directions. `union_sha` is the 12-hex sha256 stamp of presence/claims.md at the last reconcile, written by resume_variants.py --stamp; prose-level hygiene (claim containment, staleness, orphan union claims) lives in resume_variants.py, NOT here - this store is structure only. `surface` (public #59/#64, ADR-027, ADR-028) names the destination this variant targets - scripts/surfaces.py is the one lookup table (currently `print`, `public-profile`); NULLABLE here (an undeclared surface is resume_variants.py's own 'unplaced' FAIL state, not a schema violation - validate_data.py only refuses a value that IS present and not in surfaces.py's own table). `visibility` is DERIVED from `surface` by that lookup and is NEVER stored on this row - ADR-027 rejected storing it a second time. resume_variants.py --check requires a valid `surface` on every non-retired row and additionally fails 'private-on-public' on a public-surface row that prints a claim whose union bullet (presence/claims.md) carries no per-claim `[public]` tag at its head.

people._note: ADR-031 B1 — promoted from opportunities.contacts[] and channels.contacts[]. The human, once, globally unique. `title`/`cadence`/`created`/`note` are new concepts the migration never guesses at from legacy data; they start null and are filled by hand or by a later stage. jobsearch 0.91.0 (design-build-reach.md 5.2): `created` is stamped by `record.py create --file people` (the day the row was made; never typed); `employment` is the dated standing on the employer of record, `{status: current|unknown, as_of, confirmed_on?, source: stated|observed-mail|migration}` or absent, and `formerly` the past employers, `[{company_id, as_of, until?, counted_from?}]` or absent. `company_id`, `employment` and `formerly` are written only by `record.py employment|moved|merge-person`; validate_data.check_employment checks their shape.

involvements._note: ADR-031 B1 — what a person IS in one pursuit or channel: `path_type`/`role`/`status`/`note` are facts about the person IN THAT CONTEXT, never on `people`. No id of its own (design §1: 'nothing else joins to an involvement, and the pair is the identity') — unique on (person_id, opp_id|channel_id), exactly one of which is set, never both, never neither.

applications._note: ADR-031 B2 — promoted from opportunities.applications[]. `id` (= the old `app_id`, unchanged VALUE — <opp_id>-aN, still minted by record.py) is now this store's own id_field, so 'resolve this application' is a global dictionary lookup instead of an own-record array walk; the design's own words: 'promotion changes only the lookup'. `opp_id` is required (an application is always to a role; this is containment, and a plain FK is right — design §1). The three untyped legacy fields (`cover_letter`, `cover_letter_attached`, `cover_letter_doc`) do NOT survive here — a migration that cannot know a field's type must not interpret it, so where any was set on a legacy row the 0.45.0 migration creates a `cover_letters` row carrying them VERBATIM under their original names, and `cover_letter_id` points at it (`cover_letter_attached` becomes '`cover_letter_id` is non-null'). Not in 'required' on purpose: a caller never supplies `id`, the API mints it. form_answers captures what was actually answered on the form's own questions, unchanged from the pre-B2 shape: a list of {question_key, question, answer, answered_on}; validate_data.py enforces the entry shape (this file cannot express an object nested inside an array field).

proposals._note: dev #834 (jobsearch 0.86.0, design-network-first.md section 6, owner ruling 3) - one row per PROPOSAL to a prospective client, beside `applications`, several per engagement. A full-time role's path is `applications`; a fractional, interim, advisory or contract engagement (`opportunities.engagement_type` in config_keys.ENGAGEMENT_NON_EMPLOYEE) is pursued by proposal, and `opp_id` (required FK) must name one. `id` is minted `<opp_id>-pN` by `record.py proposal` (the applications pattern). `conceptual_agreement` is null or `{on, objectives[], measures[], value[]}`, each list non-empty (the client agreed what success looks like BEFORE the proposal: it confirms, it does not explore); `rate` is null or `{amount, per, currency}`. `status` is the lifecycle (drafting, sent, accepted, declined, withdrawn, expired) and `status_on` is written with every status; `date` is the day the proposal went out (the name `applications` and `touches` give that day; `sent_on` is a banned alias for it), null while drafting and required for sent, accepted, declined and expired. Every value is the CANDIDATE's: nothing writes a proposal unattended, and an accepted proposal does not end the opportunity (its own `status` stays the candidate's decision). The verbs are `record.py proposal` and `record.py proposal-status`; `conceptual_agreement` and `doc_ref` are set with `set` / `set-in`. Not to be confused with `plans.assessments[].proposals[]` (a different list: an assessment's suggested changes): user docs say "proposal rows" for this store.

cover_letters._note: ADR-031 B2 — resume_variants' twin (design §1: 'template copied, not changed'): a top-level store, a stable id, a `status` with a terminal value, a declared file where the artifact is prose. `opp_id` required (a letter is written for a role). `file` is where the authored text lives (the outreach/cover_letters.md entry, relative to the profile root — the old, untyped `cover_letter` free-text field's replacement); `doc` is the rendered artifact reference letter_out.py produces (the old `cover_letter_doc`). The 0.45.0 migration copies the three legacy applications[] fields VERBATIM under their OWN original names onto rows created here — including an inconsistent legacy row (cover_letter_attached true, cover_letter_doc null) preserved exactly as found, never resolved or guessed at.

touches._note: ADR-031 B3 — promoted from opportunities.outreach[]. `id` (= <person_id>-tN, minted by record.py — a touch is owned by the PERSON, design §1) is this store's own id_field. `person_id` is required (every outreach row already carried a resolving person_id after B1's rename; the 0.48.0 migration mints an `unresolved-<opp_id>-tN` person for any row whose person_id does not resolve, loud, never dropped). `opp_id` is OPTIONAL (public #53 — a touch to a person about no role, or anchored only to a channel, is now a legal row; the network capability's basis). `channel_id` keeps its pre-B3 meaning unchanged: the relationship the touch travelled through. `object_person_id`/`object_company_id` (design §12, both nullable FKs) name whom or what the touch is ABOUT when that differs from the recipient — an introduction ask is the concrete case. Every other field is the pre-B3 outreach[] field set, unchanged. `build_kind` (jobsearch 0.91.0, design-build-reach.md 6.2) is optional and needs no migration: `advice-ask` or `side-door`, the BUILD line a touch came from, copied from the brief row's `build` (never from drafter text) by `outbox.py detect`'s sent write (sending/detect.py BUILD_FIELDS); absent means not from a BUILD line. `validation/network_rules.check_touch_build` refuses it on the wrong touch shape; `access._open_intros` skips a `side-door` ask (an ask to a stranger is not an introduction in progress, owner O17).

outbox._note: jobsearch 0.91.0 (design-build-reach.md 9.1, 10.4, 10.5, R2 N1/N9/N13b) - one row per message that left "drafted" for the mailbox (`staged`: the candidate sends it from their own drafts) or for the candidate's approval (`queued`, email `me`: approving puts it in the drafts and the candidate sends it; jobsearch 0.93.0, ADR-043). The draft's TEXT stays in outreach/drafts.md; this store holds what a run knows about its journey to sent. `id` is `o-<n>`, minted by `outbox.py`; `draft_ref` is the drafts.md entry's `**Brief:**` id. `to` is always explicit and is the person's recorded email (or, with `reply_uid`, the address that message came from); `subject`/`body` are held ONLY while the state is queued, staged, approved or sending, and `text_sha256` (the canonical-form hash of design 10.5, sending/outbox_store.canonical_form) stays after the text is cleared. `state` moves only as sending/outbox_store.TRANSITIONS allows. `date` is the day the message was SENT, read from the sent message's own `Date:` header (named `date`, not the design's `sent_on`: `sent_on` is a banned alias for `date`). When a row becomes `sent`, ONE locked write records the `touches` row (`touch_id`), the outbound `messages` row (the sent body), marks the drafts.md entry sent, and clears the text here. `last_checked_at`/`check_result`/`none_found_checks` record send detection's own SUCCESSFUL checks (R2 N1: detection writes no `swept` row); a check that could not read the mailbox writes nothing. `approved_at` is the candidate's approval of a `me` row; `approved_session`/`sending_at` (and the `sending` state) were written only by 0.91.0-0.92.0's send path, read and never written since 0.93.0. `reply_uid` is taken from an `email-reply` draft's `**In-reply-to:** <account>:<uid>` line (B4c; sending/outbox_store.in_reply_to), and the row's `account` is that mailbox. There is no `sent_as` (R2 N13b). Since jobsearch 0.93.0 (design-resume-docx.md 6.2, 7.1) a row whose drafts.md entry carries `**Attach:** resume:<variant-id>` holds `attachments` (one item in this release: `ref` written at stage; `file` (profile-relative, "/"-separated), `sha256` and `bytes` stamped together when the draft call is printed, else null; `carried` null until `outbox.py attached` reads the saved result, true only when a result line's hash and size equal the stamp, false with `why` otherwise) and `attach_sha256` (64 hex of the refs joined by newline), the two present together or not at all, the hash checked in every state; `text_sha256` is unchanged by them (sending/attachments.py). An absent file is an empty outbox (no migration). Rules: validation/outbox_rules.py, through sending/outbox_store.check_row.

presence_changes._note: design-presence-report.md 8.2, R3 - APPEND-ONLY dated event rows about the candidate's presence copy: what the LinkedIn profile says (`stated` by the candidate, `observed` by linkedin-runner and confirmed attended), what profile-optimizer proposed for a gap (`proposal`, its claims stored verbatim), the candidate's `decision` (applied / declined, or `superseded` by a newer proposal for the same gap), and a dispatched gap key that recorded nothing (`refused`, by session, carrying exactly gap and note). No verb rewrites a row; file order is event order; `id` is `pc-<n>`, minted by record.py and strictly increasing in file order. The current value of a field is the last qualifying row in file order (presence/changes.py, the one reader). Since jobsearch 0.93.0 (design-resume-docx.md 6.1, R2 S2-2 and S2-8) a `document` row, by session on a variant target, records the team's last write or acceptance of that variant's managed Word file: `doc_op` (render, update or adopt), `file` (profile-relative, "/"-separated, ending .docx; a backslash, an absolute path or a `..` segment is refused), the fingerprints `doc_sha256`, `doc_text_sha256` and `source_sha256` (64 hex each), `ats` (failing check ids), `machine` (32 hex, or null only when the profile has no git common dir; the verb refuses null in a git profile), `written_at` (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ UTC; a document row without a readable one is refused, since it decides the newest row, never line position), and `removed`/`added` (64-hex paragraph hashes, empty unless update). It carries no value field and replay never reads it as a value. A proposal's `handback` is the hand-back file it was read from, so a consumed path is refused on a retry. An absent file is an empty store (no migration). Rules: presence/store_rules.py (validation/presence_rules.py is its facade); writers: recording/presence_verbs.py.

plans._note: ADR-031 B4 (design §10, §17) — the owner's strategy as data: a plan whose subject is a role search, a company, a person's relationship, or one bespoke opportunity. `subject_kind`/`subject_id` say what the plan is ABOUT; `opportunities.plan_id` says which plan GOVERNS a pursuit (a different question — see design §17's table). `outcomes[]` is required only on `search` plans (role|contract|access). `play_id` is a FK to `plays`, the literal `manual` (no play; the owner decides each step), or null (not yet chosen) — required only on a plan that GOVERNS pursuits (search/company/opportunity), refused on a `person` plan (design §17: 'person: governs none'). `play_confirmed` is required whenever `play_id` names a real play — an unconfirmed play acts on nothing outward (design §26.1). `goal`/`approach` are the owner's own words; no shipped code path ever writes them (ADR-031 decision 12) — null counts, never invented. `resolves_when`/`resolved_on`/`resolution` are the asks contract, copied (design §17): both-or-neither, resolution atomic with the act. `targets` is an optional override of config.json's `targets` shape, only meaningful on a `search` plan (design §26.5, owner decision 20).

assessments._note: ADR-031 B5 (design-b5-assessment.md §2) — one entry per weekly assessment of this plan, written whole by `plays.py --assess` (item C; nothing writes it before that lands). `date`/`as_of`/`window_from`/`engine_version` are the engine's; `working`/`not_working`/`next_steps`/`note` are the OWNER'S words only (`record.py assess`), never engine-written. `proposals[]` is the nested array this entry carries — declared under this entry's own `arrays` key (a list nested in a list; the dotted `fit.requirements` form addresses an OBJECT parent and cannot name it) and validated by validate_data.py's check_assessments(), which reads these two field lists rather than restating them.

proposals._note: `kind` ∈ {parameter, construct} and the KEY decides the direction mechanically (design §27.2): `parameter` → a declared parameter name of the plan's play, or `config:<dotted>` registered in config_keys.READER_KEYS — the owner's to accept; `construct` → `<signal>:<step|token>` with the signal in funnel_report.CONSTRUCT_SIGNALS — a report to the plugin team, drafted, never auto-filed (owner decision 22, pending). `evidence` keys are EXACTLY funnel_report.PROPOSAL_EVIDENCE_KEYS[kind]; an undeclared key is a validator PROBLEM. `status` ∈ {proposed, accepted, declined, reported, superseded}; `decided_on`/`decision` both-or-neither (the asks contract); `reported` is the filed issue url or null.

plays._note: ADR-031 B4 (design §18, §20) — a play IN USE by a profile: a full copy of a pattern's structure, stamped with the pattern it was copied from so a shipped improvement arrives as a reviewable diff, never a silent merge. `pattern` names the shipped `plugins/jobsearch/plays/<id>.json` this row was adopted from, or null for a hand-built play; `pattern_sha`/`pattern_reconciled_on` are the stamp (design §20). `params`/`steps`/`goal` are validated deeply by validate_data.py (the closed 15-token predicate vocabulary, the three step kinds, the closed `say` slugs) rather than by this file's generic field-list guard, the same way `comp`/`fit` on opportunities are hand-validated objects.

briefs._note: Query or Citation C1 (design-query-or-citation.md §3.3) — brief.py's own ledger: a stamped row a draft must CITE, never a source of state (§3.6 — read only by the files in brief.LEDGER_READERS: brief.py, validate_data.py, make_fixture.py and, since 0.91.0, ledger/brief_rows.py; check_ledger_reads.py is the AST gate). `id` is offset-bearing (`brief:<ISO ts with UTC offset>-<hex>`, 16 hex on a new id and 4 on rows before dev #680, D12 — a naive local timestamp orders wrongly across a DST fall-back pair). `opp_id`/`channel_id` are nullable (a brief may be person-only, folded across every thread — §3.7's AXIS_FOLD). `evidence` is `{"email": {...}, "linkedin": {...}}`, each a `{token, probes}` pair from the §4.1 vocabulary. `windows` carries the two config_keys.py values AND their provenance, printed on the card. `open_asks` is a list of asks.jsonl ids. `build` (jobsearch 0.91.0, design-build-reach.md R2 N10) is null or the BUILD step the brief was computed for, `{build_kind, play_step, touch_type, opp_id, plan_id, object_company_id, object_person_id, trigger_kind, trigger_ref}` under the touches store's own field names, derived by `reach/build.step_for` from the stores at brief time; the sent-write copies it onto the touch. Never sorted by `computed_at` — `--check` resolves only the cited id (§3.9).

source_tag._note: dev #704 / public #154 (V1). A mail source tag is `<tag>:<account>:<digits>` where <tag> is gmail, mail or ats. A uid is DIGITS: before 0.66.0 `mail_client.Mailbox.search()` handed callers bytes and every `%s` wrote the repr (`gmail:a:b'101'`), which made one message look like two. `pattern` is the clean shape, `prefix` says 'this value claims to be a mail tag', `wrapped` finds the repr of a bytes uid INSIDE a mail tag (never a bare `b'123'`: a message id minted before 0.66.0 may end in the repr, and ids are opaque, so they keep their value and are never refused for it). `fields` lists, per store, every field that can carry a tag and HOW it is checked. `whole`: the value IS a tag, or legitimately something else (`messages.source` may be a path or a LinkedIn thread URL), so only a value that starts with `prefix` must fullmatch `pattern`. `embedded`: the value, or any string nested in it, must contain no `wrapped` match: references to message ids (the fields validate_data.py resolves against messages: `messages.answers`, `touches.message_ref`, and `trigger_ref` of kind reply on touches and asks), and free text a sweep writes a dedup tag into (`asks.note`). validate_data.py reads this block and FAILS LOUDLY when it is absent, malformed or declares zero fields; a test derives the message-reference fields from the validator itself and fails if one is neither declared here nor named there with a reason. Repaired in existing profiles by migration m_0_66_0_uid_text. The run journal (`runs.jsonl`) and `inbox.jsonl` are not governed stores and are not listed: their uids are normalized when READ (journal.triaged_uids, watch.existing_keys).

banned_aliases._why: The SAME meaning under two spellings silently splits a query. Rationale: docs/adr-011-schema-enforcement.md.
